Nil T2 filing in Canada › What Happens if I Don't File a Nil T2?

The tax year stays open and the Canada Revenue Agency can demand the return and assess the corporation arbitrarily. Every resident corporation must file a T2 within six months of its fiscal year-end, every year, until it is formally dissolved. Having no revenue and no bank activity does not remove the obligation.

What Happens if I Don't File a Nil T2?

What appliesFigure
Months after the fiscal year-end to file6
Tax owing on a true nil return$0.00
Percentage late-filing penalty on a true nil return$0.00
Non-resident-owned corporation penalty$25.00 per day, to $2,500.00
How long an unfiled year stays openUntil it is filed
Fee to file$300.00 plus HST per tax year

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

A demand to file is a formal request from the Canada Revenue Agency, and an arbitrary assessment is a figure the Agency sets itself when no return arrives. Filing the real return replaces that figure with the corporation's own.

title: What Happens if I Don't File a T2 Before Dissolving My Corporation?
meta_description: Dissolution can be held up and the outstanding years remain the corporation's responsibility. A final T2 is due within six months of dissolution, and every earlier year must already be filed. An unfiled year blocks a clearance certificate, which is what confirms nothing is owed before the corporation closes.

Nil T2 filing in Canada › What Happens if I Don't File a T2 Before Dissolving My Corporation?

Dissolution can be held up and the outstanding years remain the corporation's responsibility. A final T2 is due within six months of dissolution, and every earlier year must already be filed. An unfiled year blocks a clearance certificate, which is what confirms nothing is owed before the corporation closes.

A clearance certificate confirms the corporation has no outstanding amounts before it is wound up. An unfiled year is an open year, so the certificate cannot be issued until the return is filed.
